title: kvu: a generator and measurement bench for lattice gauge theory (SU(2) Wilson action, single-source HIP/CUDA kernels, FP64 CPU reference)
description:
kvu is a Rust command-line tool for lattice gauge theory, centred on four-dimensional SU(2) Yang-Mills theory with the Wilson action. One GPU kernel source serves two backends, HIP (AMD) and CUDA (NVIDIA), compiled at run time, next to a double-precision CPU reference. Every run writes a provenance manifest (binary hash, commit, source fingerprint, seeds, options), and configurations can be archived and verified; box and fibre runs can be regenerated by `kvu regen`.

Contents: a heat-bath and overrelaxation generator with counter-based Philox4x32-10 random numbers (an FP64 reference mode and an FP32 mode; the comparison of the compat-prod mode with the anchors of the published generator su2-heatbath-gpu is described in the README, section on the state of validation on cards); Dirichlet boxes; a conditional heat bath; Wilson and Polyakov loops, gradient flow and topological charge; Balaban (L_b = 3) and Swendsen (b = 2) block-spin maps and effective-coupling estimators; the Hessian of the Wilson action on a given background; a group registry with known-answer gates (SU(2), Sp(4)). Four modules added in November 2026 are instruments: verifiable compressed archives (kvu-archive/1), couplings of a truncated effective action (plaquette, rectangle, chair, twist) by pseudo-likelihood and Schwinger-Dyson equations with jackknife errors, block-face flux statistics, and 't Hooft twisted boundary conditions (CPU FP64).

Version 0.5.1 adds, all switched off by default and described in the documentation as instruments: spectroscopy of torelons and flux tubes (CPU and GPU), a twisted-tube module, integral-method measurements on rectangular boxes (including separate couplings and a link-integrated multi-hit estimator: analytic integration of the conditional mean of a link, under the stated conditions; Parisi, Petronzio and Rapuano, Phys. Lett. B 128 (1983) 418), a replica estimator of the Renyi-2 entropy (CPU), shifted (oblique) boundary conditions, off-axis momenta, and an experiment notebook with pre-registered gates. Versions 0.2 to 0.5.0 were internal and were not published; 0.5.1 is the public version of the 0.5 line. It carries the corrections of version 0.1.1 for hard kills during thermalisation (PUB-14, including the --bord path) and for resumed runs (PUB-16); see CHANGELOG.md and docs/DEFAUTS_CONNUS.md.

It is a tool, not a physics result: it contains and claims no result on the mass gap, the continuum limit or any physical constant. The test suite (cargo test) runs on the CPU and checks documented cases (known answers, separately written Python references, deliberate mutants); it is not a general proof of correctness. Tests that need a graphics card are opt-in; they were replayed one by one from the archive on one AMD and one NVIDIA card, with the results (including failures and tests that skip themselves) reported in the README, section on the state of validation on cards. Documentation is in French.

The code was written by AI coding agents under the direction of the author. It has not been reviewed line by line by a human. See AI_USE.md.
notes: Replayed from the archive on Linux x86_64, CPU only. Developed on an AMD Radeon 8060S (gfx1151, ROCm 7.1) and an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti (sm_120, CUDA 13); state of the validation on cards for 0.5.1: see README.md, section "État de la validation sur carte (0.5.1)". See also CHANGELOG.md and AI_USE.md.
